_source_vllm: MEASURED 2026-07-28 on dgx.casa (GB10, aarch64): `du -sk -L ~/venvs/vllm-oracle` = 9542288 KiB total (9318.6 MiB); per-component from `du -sk .../site-packages/*` and `.../nvidia/*`. The venv symlink resolves to vllm-oracle-v0.25.0-stage; `python -c 'import vllm,torch'` reports vllm 0.25.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130. (The 0.26.0.dev0 pin recorded earlier is rolled back to 0.25.0 on this box; the figure names what is actually installed and measured.)
_source_ours: MEASURED 2026-07-28 on dgx.casa (GB10, aarch64, nvcc 13.0). CUDA build: `cmake -S . -B build-cuda -DVLLM_CPP_CUDA=ON -DVLLM_CPP_SERVER=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DVLLM_CPP_CUTLASS_DIR=$HOME/cutlass-4.5.0`; configure banners confirm cutlass-nvfp4 ENABLED [121a], cutlass-fp8 ENABLED [121a], FlashAttention-2 prefill/decode ENABLED [121a]. `cmake --build build-cuda --target server vllm_shared`. Server binary `strip`ped = 68974608 bytes = 65.78 MiB (`stat -c %s`, `strip`, `ls -l`). The server statically links libvllm.a, so this one file is the entire deployment; `libvllm.so` (65.66 MiB stripped) is the alternative library form of the same code, not an additional shipped file.
_source_ldd: `ldd build-cuda/examples/server` on dgx.casa: the ONLY non-system dependencies are libcudart.so.13 (707752 B = 0.67 MiB) and libcublasLt.so.13 (629945952 B = 600.76 MiB), both resolved from the SYSTEM CUDA toolkit at /usr/local/cuda-13.0 (present on any GB10 for the driver/toolkit stack). All other deps are base OS runtime (libc, libm, libstdc++, libgcc_s, libdl, libpthread, librt). vllm.cpp therefore BUNDLES 0 bytes of CUDA userspace and reuses the system CUDA runtime; vLLM instead bundles its own CUDA userspace as pip nvidia-* wheels (3144.7 MiB, counted in its bar). These system CUDA bytes are named in the footnote, not silently dropped.
_caveat: Apples-to-apple as of 2026-07-28: BOTH sides freshly measured on the same GB10. vllm.cpp is now the CUDA fast-path build (cutlass 4.5.0 + vendored FlashAttention-2 device code embedded), NOT the earlier CPU build. What you install to serve on a GB10 = one 65.8 MiB server binary; it links the system CUDA runtime (libcudart + libcublasLt, ~601 MiB) already on the box, which vLLM ships its own copies of inside the 3.07 GiB nvidia wheels.
